drhp.business: The Company manufactures and sells automotive tyres, namely farm tyres and commercial truck bias tyres, at its Ballabgarh plant. It also markets and sells passenger car tyres manufactured by Goodyear South Asia Tyres Private Limited ('GSATPL'), Aurangabad, in the replacement market, along with tubes and flaps. It serves both the Farm OE channel (tractor manufacturers) and the Farm and Consumer replacement channels, with the farm tyre business positioned as its leadership franchise.

risks.note: The Indian tyre industry is dominated by the Commercial category, which contributes more than 50% of industry revenue; the Company's limited presence there restricts portfolio selling and its ability to mitigate the risk of the Farm category.
risks.risk: Portfolio concentration in Farm with limited Commercial (Truck & Bus) presence

risks.note: Natural rubber and crude oil derivatives constitute a significant portion of tyre production costs, and fluctuations in these prices can severely impact profitability.

Erratic monsoon patterns, fluctuating reservoir levels, adverse weather and heatwaves can hit agricultural output and rural incomes, directly affecting farm tyre demand in both OE and replacement channels.
risks.risk: Dependence on the agricultural cycle and monsoon

risks.note: The ultimate parent, The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company, announced in April 2025 an intention to review all strategic, operational and financial options for the farm tire business; the review concluded on December 5, 2025 with a decision to retain ownership, but the announcement itself caused headwinds and the Farm OE segment declined -7% year-on-year.
risks.risk: Parent-level strategic review of the India farm tire business

risks.note: The Farm Replacement segment declined on account of portfolio gap and intense competition, and the Company competes aggressively for share while relying on new launches and channel expansion to close white spaces.
risks.risk: Intense competition and product portfolio gaps

risks.note: Slower than expected growth, sticky core inflation, fiscal constraints, geopolitical tension, shifts in US trade policy, reciprocal tariffs and volatile commodity prices (especially oil) are external risks flagged by management.

Management recognises that climate change poses the risk of moderate to severe physical events affecting operations and/or the supply chain, and chronic weather conditions could affect raw material supply; business continuity plans, climate risk modelling and GPSNR participation are the stated mitigants.
risks.risk: Climate change adaptation and physical/supply-chain resilience

risks.note: Uncertainty and complexity from current and emerging regulations will likely require the Company to keep evolving its manufacturing operations, use of materials and/or business model, with non-compliance capable of impacting operations and the ability to conduct business.
